subject: Re: RFP: EU→JP data transfer assurance — package and technical summary

Subject: RFP: Data transfer evidence request (EU -> JP)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our vendor RFP/assurance phase we need a short package covering how Redwood handles EU→Japan transfers for personal data. Our security and privacy team have a few specific asks: 1) copy of any executed SCCs or DPA annex you use for controller→processor transfers, 2) high-level mapping of where data is stored and how it moves (EU regions to JP), 3) technical measures for key management and access controls, 4) any DPF equivalence assessment or supplementary measures you rely on, and 5) retention and log/audit controls (time windows and retention policy).

Can you confirm you can provide this in roughly one week? Attaching our RFI doc with the exact fields we need — "MedSync_Data_Transfer_RFI_v2.docx".

Thanks,
Daniel Romero
Senior Privacy Manager
MedSync Health

Attachments:
- MedSync_Data_Transfer_RFI_v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

I'll loop Neha (privacy counsel) and Laura (security lead) to prepare the technical summary and evidence bundle. We can aim to have a short one-page technical assurance + a zip of artifacts by 11-Jul. Does that work?

Subject: RE: RFP: Data transfer evidence request (EU -> JP)

Folks — drafting notes below (will be incorporated into the package):

1) SCCs / DPA annex: we typically provide Redwood's DPA plus the SCC addendum. We do have a DocuSign envelope for SCCs when a customer requests signed execution — if MedSync requires a fully executed copy we can route it, but that adds a week for signatures. If an unsigned template + statement of execution model is OK, we can include the signed copy for prior customers as example.

2) Transfer mechanisms and DPF: we do not rely on BCRs. Our default is SCCs + documented supplementary measures (encryption in transit/at rest, KMS separation, limited geofencing, contractual controls, and audit logging). We have a short internal DPF memo that maps controls to the UK ICO/EC guidance; will include a redacted extract.

3) Technical measures: Laura will provide KMS architecture, key custody model, HSM/KMS provider, and IP allow-listing and environment isolation notes.

4) Dataflow map: confirm we only include production mapping unless MedSync explicitly asks for non-prod. Production mapping will show EMEA region storage (eu-west-1 / frankfurt) -> encrypted streaming to JP region for model inference on dedicated clusters; note that persistent PII storage remains in EU unless customer configures otherwise.

5) Retention & logs: default retention windows (audit logs 90 days by default, long-term logs for security incident support retained 2 years), configurable on Dedicated deployments. We'll make clear where Hosted vs Dedicated differ.

I'll prepare a template technical assurance page and a checklist of artifacts today. Vivek — if we need signed SCCs, flag now and we'll start the DocuSign flow.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
